questions.question: What has been abolished under Article 17 of the Constitution of India by declaring its practice a legal offence?

__
 
• **Untouchability**

 
 
• **Article 17 of the Indian Constitution of 1949** calls for the abolition of untouchability**. **
 
• **Untouchability has been eliminated**, and any form of it is prohibited.
 
• The imposition of any limitation resulting from **Untouchability is a criminal offence punishable by law.**
 
• The Act imposes** penalties (up to two years in jail)** for prohibiting anybody from entering any place of public worship or from worshipping, or denying entry to any store, public restaurant, hotel, or place of public amusement, or refusing to admit people to hospitals and refusing to sell goods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Double punishment ** 

 
 
• Prosecuted and punished for the same offence several times.
 
• This is referred to as the doctrine of double jeopardy.
 
• The Constitution prohibits twice punishment for the same crime.
 
 
 
• **Child labour**
 
 
• **Child labour refers to the exploitation of children through any form of work** that deprives children of their childhood, interferes with their ability to attend regular school, and is mentally, physically, socially and morally harmful.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment**
 
 
• Unemployment is defined as those above a certain age not working paid employment or self-employment but currently available for work during the reference period.
 
• Unemployment is measured by the unemployment rate, which is the number of people who are unemployed as a percentage of the labour force.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of perishable foods that CANNOT be stored for more than a day or two at room temperature, i.e., they have a shelf life of 1 or 2 days?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Milk__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​**

__
 
• Perishable foods 

 
 
• **Perishable foods** are those that should be stored** frozen at 0 °F or lower or refrigerated at 40 °F** or below to prevent spoilage, deterioration, or other food safety issues.** **
 
• **Meat, poultry, fish, dairy products, **and all cooked leftovers are a few examples of foods that need to be kept chilled for safety.
 
• **Bacterial growth is slowed by refrigeration.**
 
 
 
• **​**Milk
 
 
• **Milk is a priceless, nutritious meal** that needs to be handled carefully due to its short shelf life.
 
• Because it is a great environment for the growth of germs, particularly** bacterial pathogens**, which can degrade food and infect customers, **milk is highly perishable.**
 
• Due to its ability to reduce **microbial growth and milk deterioration**, hydrogen peroxide** (H2O2)** is frequently employed as a preservative in milk and** milk products. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__​​**

 
• Dried fruit 

 
 
• **Dried fruit is regarded as non-perishable** even though the majority of fresh fruits and vegetables have a short shelf life.
 
• Most dried fruit can be safely kept at **room temperature for up to a year** with proper storage, while **dried vegetables** can last around half that long.
 
 
 
• Spices
 
 
• **Spices are non-perishable foods **that can be stored at room temperature for extended periods of time without** going bad or decomposing.**
 
 
 
• **Biscuit**
 
 
• **Least perishable is the biscuit.**
 
• The least perishable items can be kept for a long period without spoiling before being** consumed or used. **

questions.question: King Porus and Alexander the Great fought which battle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Battle of Hydaspes__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​​​​​​​​​**

__
 
• Porus

 
 
• **Porus was an Indian prince** who governed the area between the** Hydaspes (Jhelum) and Acesines (Chenab) rivers** during the conquest of the Punjab by Alexander the Great (327–326 bce).** **
 
• **Porus resisted Alexander,** in contrast to his neighbour, Ambhi, king of Taxila (Takshashila).
 
• In his capacity as** King of Macedonia and Persia **and one of history's greatest military strategists, Alexander the Great built the biggest **empire the ancient world had ever known**.
 
• **Alexander the Great and King Porus **engaged in combat in the** Hydaspes in 326 BC**.
 
• It occurred along the Jhelum River's banks in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent, which the Greeks called** Hydaspes (modern-day Punjab, Pakistan).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​​​**​​​Battle of Hydaspes

 
 
• **Battle of Hydaspes **is significant because it was during this conflict in India along the banks of the **Hydaspes River **that Alexander the Great came the closest to losing.
 
• The fearless** King Porus resisted being completely subdued** by his dreaded Companion cavalry.
 
• **Alexander's career of conquest came to an end **with the defeat of Hydaspes; he passed away before beginning a new offensive.
 
• **Yogi Adityanath**, the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, said that Chandragupta Maurya, who established the Mauryan empire in the fourth century BC, had won a war against **Alexander of Macedon, **yet historians have chosen to refer to Alexander as the "great" one. 
 
• **Alexander was drawn to India because of its richness. **
 
• In addition, he was said to have a significant interest in natural history and geographic research.
 
• Before Alexander's invasion, there were numerous petty kings in northwest India,** including Ambhi of Taxila and Porus of the Jhelum region (Hydaspes). **

questions.question: The Bharhut Stupa is located in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Madhya Pradesh__.**

__
 
• Bharhut Stupa

 
 
• **Bharhut is well-known for the Buddhist stupa** (shrine) ruins that Major General** Alexander Cunningham found there in 1873**.
 
• The Indian Museum in Kolkata and the **Municipal Museum in Allahabad** currently house the majority of the stupa's sculpture remnants.
 
• The stupa was likely started during the** reign of Ashoka (c. 250 bce).**
 
• The** Mauryan king Ashoka **may have constructed the** Bharhut stupa** for the first time in the third century BCE, but many decorative elements—particularly the doorway and railings—appear to have been added during the** Shunga period**, with many reliefs dating to the **second century BCE or later.**
 
 
 
• **​Madhya Pradesh**
 
 
• Geographically,** this location is located at 23° 31' 0" North and 80° 57' 0" **East in Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• Its original name is Bharhut.
 
• From roughly **268 to 232 BCE, Ashoka the Great, **an Indian ruler of the Maurya Empire and the** son of Bindusara, **governed nearly the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• In ancient Asia,** Ashoka encouraged the spread of Buddhism.**
 
• With more than **72 million inhabitants,** Madhya Pradesh is the fifth most populous and** second-largest state** in India by area. Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Rajasthan are its neighbours to the northeast, east, south, west, and** northwest, respectively. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is located on the northern tip of India and borders** Nepal on the international side.**
 
 
 
• Bihar

 Chandragupta Maurya, a native of Magadha, established the** Mauryan Empire**, which had its beginnings there around 325 BCE.

 There was a capital. 
 
 
 
• Andhra State
 
 
• ​Andhra State and the Telugu-speaking regions of Hyderabad State were combined on November 1 to become Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The state was later divided into a new Telangana state in June 2014

questions.question: Dantidurga was associated with which of the following ruling dynasties of the early medieval India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rashtrakuta**__.

• **Dantidurga** was a ruler of the **Rashtrakuta Empire**, which existed in India from the **6th to the 10th century CE.**
 
• He was the **founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty**, which played an important role in Indian history, especially in the Deccan region.
 
• Dantidurga came to power in 735 CE after overthrowing his uncle, **Kirtivarman II,** who was ruling the Rashtrakuta kingdom at that time.
 
• Dantidurga then established his capital in** Manyakheta**, which is now known as **Malkhed **in the state of Karnataka, India.
 
• During his reign, **Dantidurga consolidated the Rashtrakuta Empire** and expanded it through military conquests.
 
• 
 
He defeated the **Chalukya and the Pallava kingdoms** and also conquered parts of the southern peninsula of India.

 

Hence, we can conclude that Dantidurga was associated with Rashtrakuta__.

 __

• Pala__
 __

• The Pala dynasty was founded by **Gopala** in the 8th century CE.

• It normally has **three primary strings**, with a fourth string serving as a drone occasionally.
 
• A** solo concerto** is a type of music in which an orchestra plays behind a single solo instrument that plays the melodic line.
 
• A **solo concerto has three movements:** a quick section, a slow section, and then another fast section.

questions.question: What is the original name of the Empress of India Act and when was it instituted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__The Royal Titles Act of 1876__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​**

__
 
• **The British Parliament approved **The Royal Titles Act 1876.** Queen Victoria was given the title of "The Empress of India"** under this Act. In that year, the Queen Victoria Proclamation was adopted. She had taken on this** title in 1876** with the support of** Benjamin Disraeli**, the** British Prime Minister.**
 
• **From 20 June 1837 until her passing in 1901**, Victoria ruled the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. Her 63-year and 7-month reign, also known as the **Victorian era.**
 
• The** reign of Queen Victoria **saw the growth of industry, advancements in education, the elimination of slavery, and improvements in **worker welfare.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of** Disraeli's well-known imperialist policies **was the** Royal Titles Act of 1876**. The British imperial title should only be used in India, it was agreed when the legislation was passed. As a result, it was first used by the** Queen in her signature in 1878**, and it first appeared on** British coins in 1893.**
 
• At the** Delhi Durbar in 1877**, she was given the formal title** Kaisar-i-Hind**, which means **"empress of India."**
 
• A** Royal Style and Titles Act**, also known as a Royal Titles Act, is an** Act of Parliament **passed in the relevant jurisdiction that establishes the formal title of the **sovereign there. **
